opening_message: There's a grass taking over a shady patch of my yard and it keeps spreading a bit more every year. Does anyone know what this actually is?

slots.name: leaf_midrib
slots.value: No, I don't see any kind of light or silvery stripe down the middle of the leaves - they're just plain green all the way across.
slots.description: Whether the leaf has the silvery midrib stripe diagnostic of Japanese stiltgrass (Microstegium vimineum) — its absence is the single fastest way to rule out the invasive and confirm whitegrass.

slots.name: stem_node_texture
slots.value: I ran my fingers along one of the stems near where a leaf comes off and it felt a little fuzzy/hairy right at that spot, not smooth.
slots.description: Node hairiness — Leersia virginica has downward-pointing hairs at the nodes, while Microstegium vimineum's nodes are glabrous (hairless). A second confirming ID feature alongside the midrib check.

slots.name: spread_pattern
slots.value: It's more like a thick clump that's gotten a bit wider each year, not really running or carpeting out across the whole yard.
slots.description: Growth habit — whitegrass forms well-defined perennial clumps via short rhizomes, distinct from stiltgrass's stoloniferous, mat-forming 'rolling carpet' spread. A clumping habit supports whitegrass over stiltgrass.

slots.name: winter_persistence
slots.value: Yeah, it's still there in the winter, just looking a bit rougher - it doesn't fully die back and disappear.
slots.description: Whitegrass is perennial and persists year-round; Japanese stiltgrass is an annual that dies back completely after first frost. Winter persistence is strong evidence against stiltgrass.

slots.name: location_in_yard
slots.value: It's in a shadier, damper spot near the back of the yard, close to where some other plants stay pretty wet.
slots.description: Habitat preference — both whitegrass and stiltgrass favor moist, partly-shaded sites, so this doesn't help distinguish between them; included as plausible background detail a homeowner would mention.

slots.name: how_long_noticed
slots.value: Been there a couple of years now, just seems to be getting a little bigger each summer.
slots.description: How long the patch has been present — doesn't change the correct identification or framing once the plant is identified; background color only.

ecological_framing_notes: Whitegrass is a native perennial grass with no invasive designation or documented ecological harm — it's part of the native understory community in moist, shaded sites. A correct answer should identify it as whitegrass (not Japanese stiltgrass), note that no herbicide or removal treatment is needed, and explain why treating it would be inappropriate (native, non-invasive, not a regulated or listed weed).
